doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: How the medicine show set up in a new town
summary: Doc went ahead for the lot and license; the troupe slept on the bus or in rooms, stayed a week or two, and assembled a portable platform.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Tell us a little about Dr. Moon's operation, right? Uh-huh. Did you say they had a platform on the back of the bus?
They had a, uh, uh, uh, kind of a stage built. Something similar to an observation platform, you know, in the back of the...
Suppose, suppose you arrive in a small town. Just tell us all the things you have to do. Suppose you drive into a place.
When we drove into a place, Doc went ahead in advance, and he got the, uh, the setup for the lot that we was going to play on, and the license here to have a license.

To play this, huh? All right, we drove, uh, we had the option to sleep on the bus if we wanted to, because he had little bunks on this bus. Uh, something similar to a brace on all over there. A car. Uh-huh. Or else we could get a room if we wanted, because medicine shows played from a week to two weeks.
Oh, you said in the town?

Most of it, mostly just a week. Uh-huh. Sometimes two weeks, though, business was real good. Uh-huh. But when we got to a town, we went directly to the, this empty lot that we was going to play. We had a portable platform that you assemble.
With a curtain, and, uh, these, these old-time, uh, carbon lights, or gas lights, or whatever you call them. We set the platform up, and we got that up.
On the back of the bus, or just, just a platform?

No, the platform was set up separate, in the lot, in the field. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. If it was any grass to be cut, we had to cut that. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. All that sort of stuff. After we set the platform up, we got our costumes on. What kind of costume did you wear?
